title: Analyst, Evergreen Portfolio Management - Private Debt
role_summary_en: Analyst in StepStone Group's Private Debt Portfolio & Risk Management team in Zurich, supporting evergreen funds through corporate-lending/private-debt data processing, market research, portfolio and performance analysis, and day-to-day fund-management support.
company_profile: StepStone Group is a global private-markets investment firm (Nasdaq: STEP). As of 30 Jun 2026 it reported about USD 913bn of total capital responsibility and USD 245bn AUM across 31 offices. Its Private Debt platform has about USD 73bn of capital responsibility and 75+ investment professionals, covering corporate, real-estate, infrastructure and specialty credit.
role_profile: Private Debt Portfolio & Risk Management analyst focused on evergreen funds. Core work is portfolio/performance analysis, market research, transaction-data processing and support to senior investment professionals rather than pure deal origination. Prior private-markets/private-debt experience is preferred, not mandatory. English fluency is required and other languages are only a plus, so there is no German-language blocker. FIT: strong investment/private-markets adjacency; main trade-off is portfolio/risk/analytics versus direct underwriting/origination.
salary_research: SALARY EXPECTATION / WHAT TO ASK: target CHF 100k base + bonus, aiming for CHF 110k+ total cash; anchor around CHF 105k base and view roughly CHF 95k base as a reasonable floor depending on bonus and pension. MARKET RESEARCH (23 Aug 2026): recent StepStone Group Analyst submissions in Zurich show total pay around CHF 92-108k and CHF 97-113k; broader Zurich StepStone data show Analyst roughly CHF 75-105k and Senior Analyst roughly CHF 105-115k. For this private-debt Analyst role, a reasonable market range is about CHF 95-110k total cash, with base likely around CHF 85-100k plus bonus. Company-specific Zurich evidence, not a generic Swiss benchmark.
salary_range: Market: CHF 95-110k total | Expectation: CHF 100k base + bonus / target CHF 110k+ total

title: Investment Risk & Analytics Specialist (Basel)
role_summary_en: Experienced investment-risk and performance-analytics role across equities, fixed income, multi-asset and alternatives. Responsibilities include ex-ante/ex-post risk analysis, VaR, tracking error, factor sensitivities, concentration and liquidity risk, performance attribution and enhancement of risk/performance frameworks.
company_profile: albedis is recruiting for an undisclosed well-established international financial-services organisation in Basel. The end client is described as highly regulated, internationally active, governance-led and stable; the employer name is not disclosed in the posting, so company-specific culture and compensation cannot yet be verified.
role_profile: Investment Risk & Analytics specialist working directly with portfolio managers and senior stakeholders. Requires several years of current hands-on investment-risk/performance experience, multi-asset portfolio analytics, Bloomberg/MSCI/Morningstar-type tools and solid Python. English is required; German is only an advantage. EU/EFTA citizenship or a valid Swiss work permit is required and the role is 100% on-site. FIT: strong on VaR, stress/risk analytics, markets, Bloomberg and quantitative investment work; the main gap to verify is depth of current Python and asset-management-specific performance attribution experience.
salary_research: SALARY EXPECTATION / WHAT TO ASK: target around CHF 125k base + bonus, aiming for roughly CHF 135k+ total; anchor near CHF 130k base and treat approximately CHF 115-120k base as the lower end depending on bonus, pension and insurance benefits. MARKET RESEARCH (23 Aug 2026): Swiss Risk Analyst compensation is roughly CHF 90-120k base / CHF 95-132k total; Senior Risk Analyst trajectory is roughly CHF 112.5-145k. Basel quantitative-analyst data show about CHF 100-145k base / CHF 110-155k total, albeit on a small sample. Given this posting explicitly asks for several years of hands-on multi-asset risk/performance analytics plus Python, a reasonable role-specific range is CHF 110-135k base plus bonus, or about CHF 120-145k total. End client is undisclosed, so this is role/location research rather than employer-specific evidence.
salary_range: Market: CHF 110-135k base + bonus (~CHF 120-145k total) | Expectation: CHF 125k base + bonus / target CHF 135k+ total

title: Financial Risk Specialist – Market & Liquidity Risk Management (w/m/d)
role_summary_en: Market and liquidity risk specialist covering Retail, Wholesale Banking and Group Treasury. The role quantifies market/liquidity risks, models customer behaviour and prepayment optionality, assesses interest-rate risk and hedging strategies, runs scenarios and stress tests, challenges models/assumptions and operates as independent Second Line risk oversight.
company_profile: ING Germany is a major direct bank and part of ING Group, with a sizeable Frankfurt platform spanning retail banking, wholesale banking, treasury and financial-risk functions. This role sits in an international risk environment with direct exposure to capital markets, Group Treasury and quantitative risk-management decisions.
role_profile: Financial Risk Specialist with a strong capital-markets and quantitative-risk focus. Requires relevant professional experience, strong capital-markets knowledge, excellent Python, analytical judgement and very good German and English. FIT: strong on market/liquidity risk, rates, hedging/derivatives, scenario analysis and model challenge. Main gaps to verify are the explicit excellent-Python requirement and whether 'very good German' is comfortable enough in practice; unlike C1/fluent wording, the posting does not explicitly state C1/C2.
salary_research: SALARY EXPECTATION / WHAT TO ASK: target EUR 90k base + bonus, aiming for around EUR 100k total; anchor around EUR 95k base and treat roughly EUR 82-85k base as a sensible floor depending on bonus/pension. MARKET RESEARCH (23 Aug 2026): ING Germany Risk Manager pay on kununu averages about EUR 96.8k gross across 17 reports. Glassdoor lists ING Financial Risk Manager in Frankfurt at roughly EUR 87-94k total with ~EUR 91k median, while broader Frankfurt financial-risk-manager data show around EUR 60-100k base plus ~EUR 10k additional pay. The role is a specialist rather than a people manager but demands capital-markets expertise and excellent Python, so EUR 80-95k base plus bonus is a reasonable role-specific range.
salary_range: Market: EUR 80-95k base + bonus (~EUR 90-105k total) | Expectation: EUR 90k base + bonus / target ~EUR 100k total

title: Investment Analyst (m/w/d)
role_summary_en: In-house international M&A and investment analyst role at ETL International. Supports buy-side transactions, business-plan and forecast analysis, valuation, transaction/document review, portfolio financial reporting and controlling, financing/capital-structure work and international stakeholder management.
company_profile: ETL International AG is the international holding company of the ETL Group, one of Germany's large professional-services networks in tax advisory, audit and legal services. The role supports ETL's international expansion and buy-side M&A programme from Essen rather than working as an external advisory analyst.
role_profile: Entry-level / early-career Investment Analyst in ETL International's management team. The posting welcomes graduates or candidates with initial experience in M&A, Corporate Finance, PE, IB, Transaction Services or Consulting and asks for strong modelling/valuation skills. Fluent English is required and good German is only an advantage. FIT: strong content-wise on buy-side M&A, valuation, modelling and financing, but seniority is clearly junior relative to an experienced candidate and some portfolio reporting/controlling is included.
salary_research: SALARY EXPECTATION / WHAT TO ASK: target EUR 65-70k base, with EUR 70k as a reasonable opening ask; treat roughly EUR 60-62k as the lower end before questioning whether the junior title is economically worthwhile. MARKET RESEARCH (23 Aug 2026): the posting itself says above-average compensation but gives no number. Kununu's Germany Investment Analyst benchmark shown on the ETL listing is about EUR 57.2k average, while a current job-board benchmark for this exact ETL role gives approximately EUR 50-70k. Because ETL labels the position Berufseinsteiger / entry-level, a realistic market range is EUR 50-70k base; asking near the top of that band is justified for a candidate bringing meaningful transaction/valuation experience.
salary_range: Market: EUR 50-70k base | Expectation: EUR 65-70k base / open at EUR 70k

title: Financial Risk Manager (m/w/d)
role_summary_en: Quantitative financial-risk role at W&W Asset Management covering valuation and validation of complex financial instruments, derivatives and structured products; global market-risk measurement and monitoring; Solvency II capital modelling; macro stress testing; review of derivative hedging strategies; and analysis of market shocks on HGB/IFRS balance-sheet positions.
company_profile: W&W Asset Management GmbH is the central asset-management and securities platform of the Wüstenrot & Württembergische Group. At 31 Dec 2025 it reported EUR 35.1bn of assets under management, placing it among Germany's 15 largest asset managers, with roughly 100 employees and more than 20 years of investment and risk-control experience. It manages group capital across fixed income, equities, alternative investments, real estate and currencies and also operates regulated fund-management capabilities, including private-debt vehicles through its Dublin platform.
role_profile: Experienced Financial Risk Manager in the asset-management risk function. The core is genuinely quantitative: pricing/validation of derivatives and structured products, market-risk modelling, stress testing, hedging review and financial-mathematics work, with Solvency II and IFRS 13 as the regulatory overlay. The posting asks for several years in financial-institution, insurance or consulting risk, a quantitative master's, and practical Python, R or SQL; FRM/CFA are explicitly a strong plus. English must be negotiation-level; the ad does not explicitly require German, although the working environment is likely German-speaking. FIT: very strong on derivatives valuation, market risk, stress testing, macro, R and FRM/CFA. Main gap is direct Solvency II / insurer-specific balance-sheet regulation rather than the quantitative finance content itself.
salary_research: SALARY EXPECTATION / WHAT TO ASK: target around EUR 95k base; I would open near EUR 100k and view roughly EUR 85-90k as the lower end depending on any variable pay, pension and benefits. MARKET RESEARCH (24 Aug 2026): XING's estimate for this exact W&W Asset Management Financial Risk Manager role is EUR 72-101.5k with an estimated midpoint around EUR 91k. W&W Group Risk Manager data on kununu average EUR 77.7k across 9 reports, with a broad EUR 61.6-117.8k range and around EUR 92.3k for 10+ years' experience. A second job-board estimate for the exact role is roughly EUR 60-81.6k, but it appears conservative versus XING and the specialist scope. Given the role's complex-derivatives valuation, quantitative modelling, several-years-experience requirement and explicit FRM/CFA preference, a realistic market range is about EUR 80-100k base, with a candidate bringing directly relevant valuation/risk credentials justified toward the upper end.
salary_range: Market: EUR 80-100k base | Expectation: EUR 95k base / open at EUR 100k
